$comment: Mission 1.76.3. The operator approved exactly one manual reply of GP-R2-B-Q1 in the existing thread. This record sits BESIDE the frozen packet, because Mission 1.66 settled that marking a frozen document APPROVED changes the artifact the operator read -- and the packet's own gate asserts it records no approval.

approval.why: an approval flag written into the frozen packet would change the bytes the operator approved, and the packet's field means THIS DOCUMENT RECORDS NO AUTHORIZATION rather than that none exists.
approval.why_it_was_recomputed_rather_than_copied: the instruction carries a digest, and copying it would make the approval name whatever the instruction said rather than whatever the packet is. Recomputing turns a quoted string into a check that could have failed.
approval.why_the_body_was_compared_and_not_assume: the instruction restated the body in full. A restatement is a claim, and this arc has already found a supplied quotation differing from stored bytes by a trailing space. The comparison is byte for byte and it passed.

approved_action.$comment: Mission 1.65's envelope rule. The digest binds the ACTION and excludes itself, the execution status, the recorded date and the recipient -- which here is not a value at all, because a reply in a thread inherits one.
approved_action.approved_subject: Terms scope: HEAD measurements of publicly reachable third-party websites

thread_binding.thread_subject: Terms scope: HEAD measurements of publicly reachable third-party websites

why_the_recipient_is_not_bound: it is not a value. The mechanism is a reply inside an established thread, which inherits its recipient, and the sender of the message being answered is still NOT_ESTABLISHED. Binding a sentinel would make the digest read as though an address had been pinned. What is bound instead is the THREAD, by three digests.

explicitly_not_authorised.$comment: The operator's own list, recorded verbatim in structure so that a later reading cannot widen this approval by forgetting what it excluded.

what_this_approval_does_not_lift.$comment: Two open things this approval leaves exactly where they were.
what_this_approval_does_not_lift.the_mailbox_read_that_would_establish_th: still unauthorised, and explicitly excluded above. The earlier sender remains NOT_ESTABLISHED, and this approval does not change that or depend on it.
what_this_approval_does_not_lift.the_attribution_of_whatever_comes_back: a reply to this reply arrives in the same thread and inherits the same problem. Approving the question does not improve the evidentiary standing of its answer.

execution.$comment: An approval says an action MAY be performed. Nothing has been performed.
execution.why_byte_verification_is_unreachable_her: Mission 1.66's ceiling, unchanged: a manual reply happens in a mail client nothing in this repository can observe. The channel is a thread rather than a fresh message and the OBSERVABILITY is identical, because the ceiling is a property of the medium.
execution.upgrade_path: NONE for this channel. A future mission may record OPERATOR_ATTESTED and nothing above it.
execution.reachable_only_through: an explicit operator attestation that the reply was sent. This repository cannot reach SENT by any other route.

relationship_to_the_spent_approvals.$comment: Two approvals precede this one and neither reaches this packet.
relationship_to_the_spent_approvals.why: it approves a different question, named by a different digest and a different question id, through a different mechanism. Nothing about the earlier two extends to it.

recommended_next_action.action: the operator sends exactly one manual reply in the existing thread, with the approved subject and the frozen body, then attests to it
